writeup.headline: Flex LNG rates Hold: very high margins offset by slipping revenue and a weak recent share price trend.
writeup.thesis: Flex LNG scores 58, a Hold, held up mainly by its quality factor (95), with a gross margin of 78.5%, an operating margin of 50.6%, no stock-based compensation and diluted share count up 0.1% year on year. Growth is the weak spot at 36: the company shows a TTM revenue decline of 2.4%, though growth sped up by 1.5 pp from the previous quarter. The trend factor sits at 45, with the price 8.1% below its 50-day average, 5.8% below its 200-day average and 15.0% below its 52-week high, and shares 16.1 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, despite shares up 36.6% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago. News risk is neutral at 50, with no guidance, analyst, legal or insider developments in the window. Balance sheet and valuation could not be scored, so the rating rests on the other four factors.
key_risks: Two vessels, Flex Artemis and Flex Volunteer, came open at the end of Q3 with no announced employment, which could weigh on revenue.
LNG spot rates were volatile in October while competitors keep adding tonnage, pressuring charter rates.
Cash covers only 0.24 times debt, leaving the company reliant on refinancing and charter income.
Revenue is already declining on a TTM basis, and analyst consensus remains Sell-leaning from earlier actions.
The share price is in a weak short-term trend, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day averages.
what_would_change: A 7-point rise in the score would reach Buy, for example from a return to revenue growth lifting the growth factor or a recovery in the share price trend.
Q3 2026 results on 2026-11-11, including any update on employment for the two open vessels, could move growth and news risk either way.
A 14-point drop would be needed for Sell, which would likely require a clear margin decline or a sharp further fall in revenue and the share price.
